newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat slips but pool price adds support.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat slips but pool price adds support.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat contracts edged back in quiet trading on Thursday following Chicago's overnight downtrend.
But brokers said the Australian Wheat Board's unexpected A$10.00 a tonne pool price increase to A$185.00 for Australian Standard White on Monday continued to support the market.
January 1997 and March 1997 both fell by 50 cents on Thursday, to A$158.00 and A$159.00 respectively, on a total of seven trades.
Cash prices stabilised on Thursday after jumping earlier in the week in response to the pool price boost.

Ed Scamps said the AWB's pool price rise still left many traders surprised. "It's a bit sudden, a bit premature," he said. Much of the maturing harvest had to compete on the world market, while the Australian dollar remained high, he said.
The market feeling was that with short-term sales commitments, the AWB needed to attract grain.
It remained to be seen whether the higher pool price could be sustained, he said.
